title: latency-adaptive-mini-chunk-prefill-with-decode-gating-and-kv-primer
author: Priya Narayanan
description:
Context and motivation: Long prefills for high context windows cause decode stalls and KV cache churn under mixed workloads (short interactive vs long-batched). Existing chunked prefill heuristics are coarse-grained and do not adapt to instantaneous latency SLO pressure or KV priming state. This PR introduces an end-to-end latency-adaptive "mini-chunk" prefill flow that breaks large prefill windows into small opportunistic mini-chunks, coordinates speculative KV priming for upcoming decode slices, and gates decode start based on a latency-aware sampler.

Design summary: The feature has three cooperating components: 1) Mini-chunk scheduler: continuous batching layer that slices prefill work into small prioritized mini-chunks (default 8-32 tokens) and schedules them across GPU streams to improve overlap with decode. Chunk size is adaptive and computed from recent token-latency distribution and SLO headroom. 2) Decode gating / sampler: a lightweight feedback loop running in the request path that decides when to start decode based on current SLO headroom, active batch occupancy, and KV primer state; it can delay decode by one or two mini-chunks to allow KV primer or kernel warmup to finish when beneficial. 3) KV primer (speculative priming): a best-effort background task that prefetches KV entries for high-confidence next-token prefixes (using a short ngram predictor) and maintains a soft TTL per context to avoid premature evictions. The primer also exposes hints to the scheduler so mini-chunks that would populate hot KV entries are prioritized.

Why this is different from previous work: Prior PRs focused on larger chunking, prefill/decode handoffs and fixed-stage overlap windowing. This change targets the micro-scheduling level: mini-chunks trade a small increase in overhead for substantially better overlap between prefill and decode and reduce tail latency variance by avoiding large single-shot prefill spikes. The adaptive sizing lets workloads with bursty short requests benefit without regressing throughput on long batched sessions.

Implementation notes: Key changes across components: - src/runtime/prefill/mini_chunk_scheduler.cpp/h: new scheduler module, token-size estimator, and queueing primitives. - src/runtime/kv/kv_primer.*: speculative primer implementation and soft TTL management. - src/runtime/scheduler/latency_sampler.cpp: SLO-aware sampler that computes headroom and advises gating. - src/runtime/ops/prefill_dispatcher.cpp: integration hooks to split prefill requests into mini-chunks and attach primer hints. - python/eval/bench/mini_chunk_bench.py: microbench harness for p95/p99 token latency and KV hit-rate. - docs/ops/mini-chunk.md: operator guide and rollout steps.

Backwards compatibility and safety: All behavior is behind a runtime flag "enable_mini_chunk_prefill" (default off in this PR for controlled rollout). The primer is best-effort and non-blocking; failures are logged and do not change request correctness. We add metrics and a conservative automatic fallback to legacy prefill when certain counters exceed safety thresholds (e.g., primer_error_rate > 0.5% or kv_miss_rate rises > 3%).

Testing and results: Extensive benching on the perf-lab across 3 model families (Llama2-13B, Red-7B, small-embed toy model) and mixed traffic templates. Representative results (lab, p95 token latency, compared to baseline): - Llama2-13B mixed interactive: p95 reduced 8.3%, p99 reduced 4.7%, throughput neutral (+0.7%). - Red-7B high-batch long contexts: throughput improved 2.4% and p95 reduced 5.1% due to better stream overlap. - Small-embed stress test: kv_miss_rate down 1.9 percentage points and prefix_latency variance down 12%. Note: microbench is deterministic but production numbers will vary; rollout uses canary gates.

Rollout plan: 1) Merge behind feature flag. 2) Enable for internal perf canary pool (10% of traffic) for 48 hours, monitor metrics (token_latency_p95, kv_miss_rate, batch_size_histogram, primer_error_rate). 3) Gradual ramp to 50% over a week if metrics stable, else roll back. An automated rollback rule is included (p95 regression > 3% for 1 hour triggers rollback).

Open items / follow-ups: - Experiment with adaptive decay for primer TTL based on model and workload (ENG-9052). - Integrate prefix-aware kernel selection hints (follow-up PR). - Add JS/TS SDK toggle for customers to opt-in.

Checklist: - [x] Implementation and unit tests - [x] Microbench harness added - [x] Docs and rollout notes - [x] Safety gates and metrics - [x] Perf numbers collected and reviewed

review_comments: Ethan Brooks (2025-03-13): Nice approach. Two asks: (1) please add a short explanation of why mini-chunk sizes default to 8-32 tokens in code comments, and (2) ensure the sampler does not spin-check busy loops; prefer event-based signals.
Priya Narayanan (2025-03-13): Addressed both. Added comments in mini_chunk_scheduler.h; sampler now subscribes to batch occupancy events instead of tight polling.

Sofia Martinez (2025-03-15): Can we get a safety net that disables primer if memory pressure spikes? Also saw one flaky test on CI, test_mini_chunk_scheduler::handles_concurrent_inserts; please investigate.
Priya Narayanan (2025-03-16): Added primer memory_pressure guard and adjusted unit test timing to remove nondeterminism. CI rerun passed.
Alex Chen (2025-03-17): Approving assuming canary monitors are ready. Suggestions: expose kv_primer.enabled as a runtime knob in ops docs for quick rollback.

release_notes: Introduce latency-adaptive mini-chunk prefill with speculative KV priming and decode gating. Opt-in via runtime flag 'enable_mini_chunk_prefill'. Improves p95 token latency on mixed workloads and reduces KV miss noise. See docs/ops/mini-chunk.md for rollout and monitoring guidance.
